biophysical_burden.boundary: The global service gap combines source hydrology, accessibility, availability, distribution and quality; it is not attributed wholly to hydrologic supply failure or urban utilities.

source_locators: WHO/UNICEF JMP 2025: 2.1 billion people lacked safely managed drinking water in 2024.
UNICEF drinking-water update: global safely managed coverage rose from 68% in 2015 to 74% in 2024.
WHO report: global trend series spans 2000-2024 and population grew from 6.2 to 8.2 billion.

transformations.formula: Use the source-reported global gap from 100 percent safely managed coverage; retain availability, accessibility and water-quality dimensions as a combined service outcome.
Normalize only the top-level population lacking safely managed service; do not add nested service-ladder categories.
Use the source-consistent 2000-2024 global monitoring interval as persistence evidence.
Divide countries with safely managed estimates by 193 UN Member States; retain the broader territories-covered count as context.
The global service gap combines source hydrology, accessibility, availability, distribution and quality; it is not attributed wholly to hydrologic supply failure or urban utilities.
0.35B + 0.30H + 0.20P + 0.15E; convert to 1-10 with 1 + 9 × composite and round to one decimal.

receipts.uncertainty: Safely managed service requires accessibility, availability and freedom from contamination; national monitoring coverage and modeled estimates vary. The gap does not isolate hydrologic supply, treatment plant capacity or raw-water quality.
receipts.freshness: JMP observation year 2024; report published 2025; snapshot reviewed 2026-08-01T16:26:59.091Z.

selection_reason.selected_method_passed: WHO/UNICEF quantifies the global safely managed drinking-water service gap, affected population, 24-year persistence and country reporting extent under the node's reviewed global service-gap contract.
higher_priority_failures: The JMP assessment does not isolate current hydrologic supply from accessibility, distribution or water-quality constraints.
No source-consistent current global utility supply-shortfall series covers magnitude, threshold and momentum.
